text: I, like so many others, picked up a box of the "new" cupcakes as soon as they hit the shelves of our grocery store. I had much of the same curiosity as others did, wondering if these improved on the previous recipe or not.  No, no it doesn't. These are ultimately the exact same cupcakes that you could buy months ago. The only difference is that the box is branded with new slogans about Hostess's come back.  These aren't bad, but they're just sort of middle of the road cupcake quality. They're nice and moist, as they were obviously made recently, but these just aren't really that exciting. The cupcake and icing are the best part of this, but the cream filling is where this falls short. It's just a little dab (not that any of you were expecting as much as there used to be) and it's so overly processed that I almost at times feel that the cupcake could have been a little better without it. If you've ever had one of these cupcakes or any of Hostess's cream filled products from about 10+ years ago, you'll know that the filling used to be much better- creamier and richer. These? Eh.  If you've loved the previous formula of cupcakes from a year or so ago, you're in luck. These are pretty much the same recipe. I was just hoping that perhaps the company would take the time to tweak these a little to where they're more than just your standard run of the mill snack cake. I'll probably buy these again in the future, but I won't run out to get them.

text: Hostess got a lot of free publicity when it declared bankruptcy and voided its obligations to pay its retired employees pensions' and healthcare obligations.  Of course the 'assets' - the factory and recipes - were quickly sold to venture capital; and employees who didn't care to be out of work along with their suddenly-evaporated non-pensions were rehired, so pretty much business as usual in the USA.  This free publicity reminded me of Hostess Cup Cakes, my favorite in the 80's.  They used to come in packs of 2, so when I saw that this was a box of 8, I thought it was a box of 8 packs of two.  Nope, it's a box of 8 single cupcakes, each one individually wrapped.  They're also about half the size they were in the 80s - if that - and they are not packaged in plastic cups any more, just sitting on a cardstock board, so they are sort of squashy and get molded roughly into a cube shape on their journey to your house.  They tasted just like I remember 'em; moist cake, rich chocolate flavor, creamy icing, and of course that white foam, reminiscent of Chantilly cream, in the middle.  They arrived a few days before their sell-by date and freshness was not in question; they tasted fine.  I am not sure I am really on board with a buck fifty apiece for such tiny morsels - I can get larger, fresher, less technologically engineered cupcakes at that price at the local bakery - but otherwise, these cakes deliver as expected.
title: Hostess is back on-line

The coffee capsules are not Keurig licensed, but outwardly look the same as Keurig licensed K-cups, and work the same. A case of them are packed loose in the box. text: When talking about "strong" coffee, there are two major aspects of what "strong" means. One aspect is the intensity of the coffee's roasted flavor. The other major aspect is the intensity/level of caffeine in the coffee.  Both of these aspects start with the coffee variety.  The level/strength of caffeine in a coffee is dependent, primarily, on the coffee's inherent, natural, level of caffeine.  For example, Kenyan AAA coffee is a coffee variety that is naturally higher in caffeine level.  How a coffee is roasted also affects the level of natural caffeine in the coffee.  Darker roasts actually LOWER the level of caffeine in any variety of coffee.  For example, let's consider Kenyan AAA.  In a "light roast", that coffee will have the highest level of caffeine when brewed.  If a Kenyan AAA is roasted to be dark, there will be LESS caffeine in that brewed coffee.  The lighter any coffee bean is roasted, the higher level of caffeine remains in the brewed product.  The darker any coffee bean is roasted, the LOWER the level of caffeine in the brewed product.  So, when a coffee roaster, like this one, claims to be, "The strongest coffee", it means it has a strong roasted flavor, not a strong or high level of caffeine.  If the same coffee beans in this coffee were roasted to a lighter or medium roast, that coffee would have MORE caffeine than the dark roasted version.  For me, I greatly prefer a medium roast, as that results in more balanced flavor that retains more of its natural ca
title: Dark Roast is strong flavor, not stronger in caffeine!

text: Another Top 100 Favorite Products:  How in the world could anyone not love Fritos? - that is the question.  I've eaten these nearly all my life having worked in the fields of California and Oregon during my youth from 4th grade through 12th grade during the summer months, along with my farm laborer father who always made sure we had a nice hearty lunch which often included Fritos.  Yep, regardless of whether or not, we had bologna, pressed ham, egg or other types of sandwiches, Fritos were often included in our lunch sacks.  I'll never forget those sweet summer days where our entire family gathered under the cherry trees in The Dalles, Oregon, or in the bean fields around Stayton, Oregon and ate our lunch together.  Some folks may think it was a hard life, but I thought it was a wonderful life - the entire family working together to earn enough money during the summer to purchase school clothes and help supplement the family funds to get us through the fall, winter and spring.  Those years are long past, but Fritos remain in my life. It's been years and years since I've worked in the fields or orchards, but I do make tuna sandwiches and inevitably, Fritos accompany those sandwiches - difference being - now they're shared with my husband.  The ingredient list is simple:  Corn, Corn Oil, and Salt.  In this day and age of nearly every packaged food being full of added ingredients, Fritos remain a fairly simple food.  One of a kind. text: In the beginning, God created coffee.  It percolated, and Mrs. Olsen told the neighbors to buy Folger's.  Then came The Apostle Joe Dimaggio and Mr. Coffee, and Lo, we filtered water through a piece of paper that drove you crazy trying to just pick up ONE and not a handful.  And life was good.  And then, java junkies, along came Saint Keurig.  And the people rejoiced.  Now comes Brooklyn Beans' Variety Pack - and now it's YOUR turn to rejoice.  There's not a clinker in the bunch here.  I consider myself something of a coffee freak (some would just say plain ol' freak) and I know when a company is repackaging the same dreck in a fancy new box (Green Mountain, I'm looking at you) and when people CARE about what they're producing and are dedicated to making a GREAT product.  I'm the only coffee drinker in my house (they're all mine!  Mine, I tell you!  Bwahahaha!) and I've gone thru this entire box and found several that are now all-time favorites, but again, there's not a bad cup to be found here.  The Brooklyn guys know their stuff, and they make a great cup o' joe.  Light roast, medium, dark, flavored - whatever your preference, there's a bunch of Brooklyn options for you. text: Though I never bought this item from Amazon, these have been my most favorite packaged noodles by far for more than a decade, and today my taste buds feel vindicated after finding out that it's the number one best seller on Amazon. I have tried a few other noodles out of curiosity, always in the hope of discovering better or other great-tasting pre-packaged noodles, but have never found anything close to it. That said, I have not really tried out a large number of other varieties of noodles and I also came across The Ramen Rater website today and do plan to try out his all time best packages over the next few months .. but I digress.  While I like its extra-hot spicy taste, I usually add the following ingredients (sparingly, so as not to overwhelm its original taste): shrimp, green hot serrano chili peppers, button mushrooms, frozen peas, a few slices of chopped tomatoes, garlic, ginger, Chinese parsley (a k a coriander leaves or Cilantro) and last but not the least, my own secret ingredient - a few tablespoons of ready-made Tom Yum Paste which I buy from Asian grocery stores. Sometimes I also add lime juice and or lemon / lime zest at the end if I want a slightly sour taste. These ingredients, especially the Tom Yum paste even make far lesser noodles like [[ASIN:B003OB2DM0 Maruchan Instant Lunch, Hot and Spicy Shrimp, 2.25-Ounce Packages (Pack of 12)]] - which are sold by Walmart for about thirty cents per cup - taste almost (but not quite) as good.

text: I grew up on peppermint tea, and honey lemon tea. That's it. That is the only tea in my parents house while I was growing up. It wasn't until I grew up and moved out that I decided to try other flavors.  I went with this sample pack due to the high ratings, large number of samples to choose from,  and the fact that each sample was a single serving (perfect so that if you dislike one, it's fine because it's literally one serving only).  I didn't realize until it arrived in the mail but it also comes with a menu with all the flavors. I kept this chart and have been marking my own ratings next to each one so I remember what I should, or should not, buy again in larger quantity.  I would also like to mention the quality of this tea. Each time I open up a new packet, the scent of the tea leaves is so amazingly fresh! I will never,  ever go back to tea bags. Loose leaf teas, preferably this brand, is the way to go. It's no wonder why the ratings are so high!  Overall, I'm highly satisfied. If you're looking to expand your taste on teas, buy this! You'd be surprised what flavors you normally wouldn't try are like. So far my favorite is blueberry merlot, and this is coming from someone who hates blueberry flavored anything. I would have never picked up this flavor had it been by itself, but now I will thanks to this sample pack that surprised me!

text: Harney sells a multitude of different products all called Hot Cinnamon Tea. It is very confusing for anyone to understand the difference as they are all called the same thing, and in one instance they use the name Hot Cinnamon Spice. I had this flavor tea somewhere and I liked it so I ordered this thinking it was the same thing after looking at all of the options. Various tins, boxes etc all looking and sounding the same. Well they are not.  At least in this instance and after contacting Harneys customer service I was told that there are tea satchels and tea bags. DO NOT order the tea bags as they are not very good, or at least not any better than any cinnamon tea product that you can buy at your local Krogers, Publix or health food store. Just very disappointing and it casts a shadow over why they market their products like this. Certainly makes me suspicious.  There really is no need for playing name games. Although I liked the tea satchels and that is what I was looking for originally, I will look elsewhere for a good cinnamon tea from in my opinion, a more reputable company.

text: This makes an absolutely wonderful espresso. Rich, flavorful with chocolate notes and a nice lingering aftertaste. As the name suggests, the crema production is excellent.  It's also, like most Lavazza beans, a pretty forgiving bean. Even if you don't hit the exact right temperature or are a bit off in your grind or dose, it will still produce a decent cup. Of course, if you nail the prep you'll get an outstanding cup, but it's not as finicky as other beans I've used.  It also blends well with Lavazza Dek if you want to do a half-caf.  Although I use this mainly for espresso, I also tried it as a pour-over and in a french press. Both turned out very nice, especially the french press.  As with all Lavazza beans, it is a medium roast, which is the classic Northern Italian style. If you want a dark, oily bean, you won't be happy with this. I greatly prefer a medium roast since I never use milk in my espresso, and the medium roast allows all the flavors to come through without the heavy, burnt taste that's typical with dark roasts.  Highly recommend!
title: Excellent Northern Italian-style espresso

text: I bought this gum to emulate what it was like to chew "real" chewing gum from back in the day, and it blew me away.  The small bump of caffeine is a really nice touch.  Being a larger person, I pop about three pieces in to "get the best experience".  I think this stuff is worth the money, but I have to take it easy with it.  Since the gum has real sugar in it, overdoing it may cause teeth problems.  Would definitely buy again.  My only concern is that I bought such a large pack, I don't know if it will still be fresh by the time I get to the last pack.  To summarize the chewing experience, it starts off quite stiff, but loosens as it warms up in your mouth.  The real gum in it gives it a looser chewing experience than modern day chewing gums, which I like.  You can still blow bubbles with it but be warned: if you get this in your beard, your going to have a bad time.  I almost had a mishap but it came out with a few minutes of picking.  The flavor is great and lasts a little less than modern day chewing gum.  This gum does not get hard from extended usage periods.  The packs even come with spit wad papers, which I recommend using.  This gum gives me the feeling it would be a lot harder to clean up if stepped on or if it gets in hair.
title: Nostalgic

text: This gum is the best I've ever had. I got a variety pack of the Boost, Revive, and Cleanse flavors. The gum base definitely does feel different in the mouth than the other gums, and for me that's neither or good or bad thing. That's just how the gum is. It feels nice to know I am chewing on chicle rather than plastic, so that's definitely great! However, what I really like about this gum is the flavor. It tastes very whole, very natural. My favorite is the lemongrass, turmeric, cayenne flavor. It's definitely a bit spicy, and it tastes strongly of lemongrass oil. It has a much more "full" flavor than a lemon candy might. Each of the gums in this variety pack contain cayenne pepper, and it's not something I'd thought of to put in gum, but it really, really works. Long after the initial flavor is gone, the cayenne remains present, keeping a general "warm" feeling in my mouth. It makes the gum pleasant to chew for a long time, long after I'd have spat out most fruit flavored gums. I've never enjoyed harsh mint, but they seemed like the only gums that would last... until now! This is a quite pricey gum, but I think it's worth it- I paid $15 for a pack of six boxes, each containing 15 pieces, and I think at that price the pleasure the gum brings is worth it. It's definitely a more enjoyable experience than any other gum I've ever tried, and for that, I'll be buying this again. I might experiment with a different flavor though- the maple looks intriguing! 5 stars to Simply Gum. Gre

text: Natural Flavor Ingredient is NOT natural. In addition to their original flavor source, these mixtures can contain more than 100 different chemicals, including preservatives, solvents and other substances. text: Like the taste, honestly couldn't care less about the color, although I guess some people think it's pretty...  Initially, I thought this seemed 'saltier' than the regular white sea salt that we'd been using in our grinders. And I like that, 'cause -- let's face it, a lot of us love salty foods, despite their dubious effects on our health. I have been eating far more healthfully in recent years, though, and have also cut my salt consumption, to the point that I have learned to enjoy some things without salt that I used to really love WITH it. (Watermelon, for example...)  After using this salt for several months, I don't think it's really 'saltier' anymore. I think that it's softer -- literally -- and grinds more easily, resulting in heavier portions as it falls off the grinder. With typical white sea salt, I find it fairly easy to vary the grind, so much that there can be a discernible grit to coarser settings. It doesn't seem to matter where I set the grinder wheel using this salt -- the result remains a fairly consistent powder. I can't really force a coarse grind, no matter how much I loosen the wheel. So I'm guessing that I'm actually using more, and it's evidenced by the fact that we're plowing through the first bag much more quickly than anticipated.  Tastes great, though. Would buy again.
title: A Great-Tasting, Colorful Product

text: This makes fantastic iced tea as well. I've been trying to find an iced tea that comes out clear without much hassle. Lipton, Luzianne, Tetley - all these teas are a bit finicky when trying to brew just right. On occasion if you overbrew you get a cloudy, mucky mess of a tea. And I like my iced tea to be clear as highly polished amber. This one is so hard to mess up. I use four bags in a pyrex measuring cup. I can walk away from it while it's steeping. Somewhere after 6 minutes or so I check on it. Then I pour it over ice. I've tried to take pictures of how it looks, but it's frosting the pitcher so it's hard to tell how nice it looks. I know people might be like, who cares how it looks? But often cloudy tea has a horrible taste to it. Very bitter.  This also tastes great. It has a nice sharp flavor to it without being too much. I found I had to get used to it, the first couple of glasses I was expecting the more mellow taste of more basic iced teas. Once I did get used to the change, I will not go back. This is my new iced tea!

I love exotic teas, and I'm very open to all sorts of new flavors and complex flavor combinations.  But this?  This was awful:  the smoke literally tastes like someone steeped a bunch of cigarette butts and made a tea out of it.  I mean, not quite THAT bad but close, and literally sickening--it felt like I had been around a bunch of 2nd-hand smoke after even just opening the box, and especially after consuming half a mug of this tea--I had to throw the rest of the mug out, and I gave my box away to the person who recommended it to me.  So I gave this one star, because, again, it is the single most sickening thing I've ever consumed (food or drink).  Yet, while I share that with you to warn you, in case you might have the same experience upon trying it, I also feel compelled to add, in fairness, that it seems to be a high quality tea--the ingredients are just "black tea" (which seems to be fine black tea) and "smoke".  It's that latter ingredient where the AWFULNESS comes in, yet apparently it is made with a high quality smoke, if you will, from pine wood and bamboo (mainly the pine is what the smoke is from--they place the tea leaves on bamboo and then smoke it with pine). text: Much has been written about how great this product is and of all kinds of benefits it has, so there is no need to elaborate on that, other than add my vote to it. The purpose of this review is sharing some practical usage and storage tips with the "newbies" so you don't accidentally waste and have to throw away your supply.  There are smaller packages of Dandy blend available even here on Amazon, however economically this size makes best practical sense, as it's the least expensive (price per oz) option, provided you will store it right. The instruction on the label say that Dandelion is sensitive to moisture and the bag needs to be resealed completely after each use.  However I found out that itself is not enough (I live in area with high humidity).  From my experience, the best thing to do if you buy this size is to either share it with a friend and/or do the following:  I put mine in a small size glass mason jar with a lid and store it in the fridge (or even freezer, either way). What is left, stays in the original bag, gets sealed, put in additional Ziploc bag and stored in the freezer.  There it will last quite a long time. What happens if you leave it at room temperature is, it absorbs moisture and hardens into a block pretty quickly, and you have to literally chisel it to break a piece off, plus it dissolves lot harder and loses some original flavor, so it pretty much gets ruined. text: This is a really good coffee substitute.  It does not have the richness or "body" of coffee, but it also doesn't have the acidity or caffeine.  I like the taste very much.  However, I do recommend following the package instructions on how much to use: 1 level teaspoon per 8 ounces water makes a "tea-like beverage 1 rounded teaspoon per 8 ounces of water makes "rich, full-bodied coffee" 1 heaping teaspoon up to 1 tablespoon for an 'espresso strength beverage".  I was using *at least* a tablespoon in a 12 ounce mug.  It makes a really tasty espresso-like drink, but I started having gastrointestinal issues with just one mug a day.  I did a little research, and discovered that one ingredient, dandelion, can have a laxative effect; another ingredient, chicory, contains inulin, a carbohydrate fiber (an oligosaccharide) which can be hard to digest.  I dialed back the amount I was using, and didn't have further problems.  I don't fault the product at all; it was my own overzealous use of it that caused problems.  Again, using the recommended amount (1 rounded teaspoon) per mug has been fine.

text: I was just as anxious as a child on Christmas waiting for the package to arrive, the package that contained my order of Death Wish Coffee. My fellow colleagues are already subscription holders of this very pristine brand of coffee. My first impression of this coffee was it's subtle yet bold taste not at all over barring, then it happened the sky turned red and the clouds black, I was holding a Battle Axe it Bears the Insignia of Death Wish Coffee. I was wearing matt black body armor, my senses are then dialed to 100. Then I heard it..... A Battle cry it was incredible I knew what i had to do, a elephant the size of semi truck stepped out of the tree line he spoke to me "it's time" he said it not from his mouth but telepathically my heart began to race. I felt the sudden urge to defend my honor and life, I mounted the elephant and we rode the hillside where it stood. a hoard that beckoned to be slaughtered, the elephant rode with me mounted on his back, by the dozens they fell. goblins wearing bad brands of coffee on there poorly made armor, then I stood proud on top of the smoldering bodies. I knew then this was my path to follow. The Axe glowed a proud red the elephant let out a roar so loud the ground shook the trees shook the sky rumbled and then the elephant spoke again this is your path to follow. Yes Death Wish is my new way to escape the world as I know it.
title: A New World

It simply has more flavor, and while the flavor ain’t exactly GREAT, it’s got a measure of depth and complexity and a bit of acidity you don’t really expect in a Robusta-heavy blend.  The beans were also quite fresh when I received them (as a gift,) bubbling up quite strongly when hot water was first applied.  I prepared it using a French press and Aeropress and preferred the latter, in part because I think it moderates the caffeine a bit. The caffeine, not taste, is what this coffee  is all about, obviously, and it lives up to its billing. Two cups gave me a headache on a normal morning, although I imagine it would be just the ticket some days.  I compensated by drinking less of it, but I actually like drinking a lot of coffee and am not interested in kicking physical dependence to a new level.

text: Ok, reviewing whole bean coffee. That is a can of worms, especially considering the spectrum of what ppl consider "good" coffee.(I personally can never understand how Starbucks makes any money at all as I think their coffee is over roasted and consequently tastes burnt to me. That said, perhaps you will have some insight to what I consider good, a medium roast with a full body with low acid. Normally I buy the 100% Columbian from Sam's Club (2.5lbs for $14.48) and really enjoy it. Unfortunately I was out and had to get a substitute (visiting  a friend over the holidaze) and looked high and low for reviews, reccomendations et al. Long story short, settled on 8 o'clock, brought it home, brewed it up... and nothing. The taste was flat as if the beans had sat in a warehouse for years. There was zero I liked about it and within 3 days of drinking the stuff, I drove the 80+ miles to the nearest Sam's Club, bought 5 lbs of beans and drove back. I even tried mixing some of the 8 o'clock coffee with the Sam's; it just highligted the "chalkiness" and blandness of the coffee. Needless to say I have just under two lbs of 8 o'chalk Coffee to give to anyone who wants it. Go Sam's Club. But in the end, everybody has to make their own decision.

These noodles taste like this. I decided to try the milk soaking technique recommended don the package. I used almond milk that was unsweetened and unflavored. Then the  noodles tasted like the almond milk! I was going to use them with my spaghetti sauce, so I would have rather had them taste like olives :-)  I soaked them again, in hot water with a splash of vinegar, then rinsed, and they were not as almond tasting. I simmer them, as recommended, if one prefers a softer noodle. They worked just fine with my spaghetti sauce, and have almost no calories. When I try my second pan, I think I will forego the milk soaking, and just simmer and rinse. I will plan on incorporating their nature; flavor into whatever I make - after all, I love  olives!

text: So i usually get truff from the local market as I save a couple bucks, as I’ll continue to do. I wasn’t impressed with it at first—it was far too sweet for my liking, but as a chef I could appreciate every nuance that comes with this sauce. Truffles are hit or miss, you either hate them or love them, and if you hate them, this sauce is not for you. The nose will bother you as it’s very pungent and truffle forward, the taste will horrify you as it can come off as overwhelming with every drop. As i mentioned before, AT FIRST i was far from impressed with this sauce, I couldn’t use it in the ways that i as a fan of heat and hot sauces would normally use hot sauces, it wasn’t what i expect from hot sauces and to be fair, i wouldn’t classify something thats not hot at all like this as a hot sauce. I couldn’t fold it into  my aioli, i couldn’t make interesting mayos with it that my pallet agreed with, i couldn’t put it on wings as there are just far better options for wing sauces, and I couldn’t shake it up in a bag of mangos as the acid from the mangos almost completely nullifies the truffle flavor and youre just left with the odd repulsive smell of fruity truffles (trust me, it’s a gross smell). And then one day, i accidentally tipped the jar over, and due to the leaky cap that everyone keeps mentioning, it got on my pizza, and as an NYC native who loves  pizza, I WAS IN HEAVEN!

text: I decided to try this Harney & Sons Black Earl Grey Loose Leaf Tea for the first time and I'm very disappointed based on the other positive reviews. Most earl grey's recommend 1 teaspoon of tea per cup and 3 minutes steeping time, but this Harney & Sons tin says to use 2 teaspoons and steep for 5 minutes. That was a bad sign for me even before the first cup. Even so, I followed the instructions and it basically tastes like hot water with a very slight taste of tea. I cannot taste any hint of bergamot, nor when I smell the tin of tea there is no bergamot smell (and barely even notice a tea smell). Also, don't use a tea ball, as there are too many fines. Twice now I've used a ball and the cup is full of tea floating around. So use a fine strainer if you risk this tea. If I could, I'd return the tea for what this is, but will probably just throw it away in the trash. While I have other teas in my cupboard, nothing is like a good cup of earl grey and I'm sad that I'll need to look elsewhere to replenish my supply.

text: I have been receiving this product for almost a year as a subscribe and save deal. Up until a few months ago Amazon sent the real, original thing. This is unfortunately no longer the case! If you order this you will get Ito En Oi Ocha, yes...but it's made in Thailand and comes in a really weak, pathetic bottle. Ito En HAS NOT changed their suppliers or changed their factory locations completely to Thailand. They still manufacture this product in Japan. Amazon has simply decided to buy the cheaper Thai version of the product, likely due to the strength of the Yen...but I would still gladly pay more to get the original thing...  As far as the flavor goes, the Thai version tastes a different, likely due to the taste difference of Thai water vs. Japanese water. You cannot tell if it is VERY cold...but if it is above fridge temperature you can definitely taste (*and even smell!*) a difference.  Amazon's image for the product is WRONG. That is not the product you will receive.  Unless you have no other options to get this product DO NOT BUY IT until Amazon understands that sourcing "Japanese" green tea from Thailand is wrong and an insult to their customers.

text: I bought the 30 mini-bag box of Goldfish...received September 13, 2018.  The plan was to send most of these to my kids in a "Birthday Box" of various items for Late October. Problem is...the "Sell By" date is November 18, 2018..... Now..I don't know if "Sell By" means 'stale by'....but I figure the sell by date doesn't give you more than weeks to eat them.... So...let's do the math...bought 9-13-18...sell by 11-18-18...that is roughly 65 days...on a Box with 30 units in it. That means that one person would have to eat roughly ONE snack bag EVERY OTHER Day... Or...if I send 20 bags for late October...each kid gets 10...to eat in 18 days...that's MORE than ONE every other day. Bottom Line:  Nobody eats a bag of Goldfish EVERY OTHER day for 2 months.... Bottom Bottom Line: I'll get my snacks at the Grocery store again...where I can SEE the expiration date.  Side note: The food industry should standardize expiration dates.... there's Sell By...best if used by....best by...Enjoy By....and other products just with a Date...like Milk.... I think all products should use "Get sick after" (date).......ie...let us know when NOT to Eat the stuff...  Update September 17, 2018.... Went to the Grocery store...checked out the huge cartons of Goldfish...Expiration date 4-10-2019.. ie..more than 7 months from now...geez.. Bottom bottom bottom line....I'm right...they sent me "end of life" product.
title: "Sell by" date too soon

text: My first two experiences with ordering this product were great; the expiration dates of the cartons that I received were 8 months out in advance, and the flavor of the product itself was as expected. My most recent order, however, was disappointing.  I received two cartons that are set to expire 4 months from now (They were manufactured in September 2021, expire in May 2022, and I received them on January 19, 2022.) Initially, I was upset by this because 60 oz of Goldfish is too much for one person to eat within just a few months, but I brushed it off because I thought that the taste of the crackers would at least make up for this inconvenience. Well, I was wrong. To make matters worse, the crackers taste off. It's not that they're stale but rather that they don't have a distinctive cheese flavor. They're plain, and the only flavors that I'm able to pick up on are salt, yeast, and a slightly burnt taste. I had my mom try some to get her opinion, and she agreed that they don't taste all that good. She compared them to off-brand Goldfish and even asked if I was sure that they were the real deal.  I don't think that I'm able to return my order since most food items are non-returnable, and I already opened up one of the cartons. Like I said, the first two times that I ordered this product, I had no complaints, but this recent order was not worth the almost $10 that I spent on it. Now, I'm stuck with a bunch of flavorless crackers that are going to expire within the next few month

text: This review is for Bigelow Earl Grey Black Tea, Caffeinated, 20 Count (Pack of 6). I really love drinking hot earl grey black tea in the mornings for breakfast. I usually add milk and sometimes honey depending on what I’m eating for breakfast. I love that this comes in a 6-pack with a subscription option because I drink 2 cups of it per day which depletes my stash pretty quickly. What makes it nice also is that it is individually sealed so that I can take some with me to the office if I’m running late. I think it also tastes fresher when individually sealed and not in one giant pouch. It has enough caffeine to wake me up but not keep me on edge like coffee usually does. The bergamot oil is supposedly from Calabria, Italy but I’m not entirely sure where the black tea is sourced (hope it’s not China!) and then blended and packaged in the USA. Nevertheless, I really enjoy this blend from Bigelow. The aroma is just perfect and not overpowering. I’ve had earl grey teas from other brands but always come back to Bigelow. If I only knew the source of the black tea though, I’d be much happier. Overall, I think this is a great tea all around and I would definitely recommend their earl grey black tea. I’d give it 4.8/5.0 - 09/11/2022.

text: I ordered these with high hopes.  I love the Mission Pork Rinds that are pre-popped at the store.  I was hoping for a similar taste.  Unfortunately, these pork rinds were just gross.  These are my issues: 1) Wow!  These are really salty.  I am sensitive to salt, but OMG, gross salty.  2) After popping and eating these, I noticed that they sort of melted in my mouth and stuck to my teeth as a sort of gummy paste that I had to pick out.  Again, gross.  3)  They smell terrible when they are cooking.  It was hard for me to get over the smell.  One reviewer said she likes them as nachos.  So, in an attempt to salvage these pork rinds, I melted some cheese over them and topped them with salsa and sour cream.  For the first few bites, I thought they were just okay, but then I realized, nope, still gross.  Luckily, my dog likes them.  So now she has 16 more packages of pork rinds to eat.  But, I did notice after she polished off the bowl that she was making weird faces and licking a lot and I realized, ah, she's having the gummy teeth feeling too.  Just ewwww!

text: As someone who loves popcorn and has tried countless seasonings, I can confidently say that Flavacol is a game-changer. It's amazing how such a small addition can transform a bowl of plain popcorn into a delicious treat that's impossible to resist.  The secret is in the fine salt flakes that cling perfectly to the popcorn, ensuring that every kernel is coated in flavor.  I love that it is easy to use, and a little goes a long way. With just a few sprinkles, I can turn a boring batch of popcorn into a snack that everyone wants to try. I've even found myself experimenting with different toppings to take my popcorn to the next level.  This is a must-have for anyone who wants to elevate their popcorn game. I feel betrayed and a little cheated, as I would pay more for more actual lemon or lime crystals. text: Bought this for baking without sugar.  Love Monk Fruit as a sweetener.  Love the taste and it has a lovely sweetness.  I realize Lakanto is trying to cut it with something to make it a 1 to 1 match with sugar for baking etc... It doesn't quite work in my opinion.  They need to add more monk fruit and reduce the erythritol.  Erythritol has a strange coolness to it that is very noticeable in the end product.  I ended up having to add a bit of honey to mask the effect of the erythrotol.  I also think that more monk fruit in the mix would have been a better choice since my end product was less sweet once baked than expected.  I could have added more Lakanto sweetener but then I'd have to deal with the additional problem of the erythritol effect requiring more alternate masking flavors.  I will continue to use this and add raw monk fruit powder when I can get it to make a sweeter blend that works better in baking.  Monk fruit has a slight camelish flavor that works well with some types of baking (such as products that use brown sugar, dried fruits and spices).  I would recommend using it to anyone that must find an alternative to sugar.

text: First off, all of the San Pellegrino Sparkling fruit beverages are fantastic Italian style sodas!  I only wish Amazon would carry the San Pellegrino Chinotto (bitter orange flavor Italian soda), as it seems this flavor in particular is quite hard to find. In fact I can't find it at a decent price and in large quantities at all within a 110 mile radius of my city!  Now I must say that the price was right for this product when I ordered it, but the shipping method didn't work out so well. The box was pretty beat-up, the corners seemed crushed and the walls were bending. The box was really a little too big and the bubble-padding material was either popped during shipment or not inflated when it was packed. For a product like this, it should be properly padded, as these types of carbonated beverages can explode or leak when the cans get dropped or dented.  Many of the cans were dented. In fact I wouldn't be surprised if the package was dropped or had heavier boxes on top of it.  The carrier may have had no idea what was inside, but Amazon did.  I felt lucky that none of the beverages exploded or leaked, being that most of them were dented around the edges of the tops and bottoms. Maybe this was just a problem with my individual shipment? It is just soda, but I think it deserves to arrive in new condition like any other item and not banged up.  Overall, this product is wonderful. I would consider ordering it again as long as the price is comparable to buying it locally, but I hope

text: I've been eating Chocolate Coconut Chew Larabars daily for over 5 years.  When the bars are relatively fresh, they are delicious and 5+ stars.  The problem is that it has become increasingly difficult to purchase fresh bars.  How fresh or stale they taste is directly related to the "Best By" date stamped beneath the seam/flap on each bar.  I have seen dates as much as 12 months in the future so I tend to assume that when manufactured, they are stamped one year into the future.  My experience is that bars with 9+ months to go on the "Best By" date taste fresh and completely different from older bars, which taste stale - you need to taste a fresher bar to understand this.  In particular, the almonds taste stale (rancid?).  This issue has only arisen in the last 6-9 months - it was fairly easy to source fresh bars before then.  On my recent shipments from Amazon, the "Best By" dates were 5-6 months in the future.  These bars have been sitting on a shelf somewhere for 6-7 months and they taste like it.  I've tried very hard to find a reliable source of fresher Larabars online and locally and have unfortunately failed.  I am switching over to Kind bars which are consistently much fresher.  Posted with regrets, since this is potentially such a great product but the way Larabar distribution is handled must be spoiling it.  BTW, I've written Larabar several times and all they do is send me some free coupons and the problem continues.
title: Beware of stale tasting Chocolate Coconut Chew Larabars

text: The company emailed me and asked for a review. Unlike some 1-star reviews, my package arrived (to Panama) intact. The company asked me to notify them if the product "didn't work." I don't know how to answer that. I bought the chia seeds because I take supplements and things that are supposed to be "good for me," along with eating what I consider a healthful diet, so I haven't noticed any difference. I do believe that chia seeds are beneficial.  I'm giving this product 4 stars because I have questions about the origin and certification. Although it says "Raw, USDA Organic, Certified Non-GMO," etc., the package also says "product of Mexico/Argentina/Paraguay."  With the seeds being grown in either of these different countries, how is the certification possible and/or reliable? I'm not saying the certification is false. I'm just wondering.  Also, I don't trust anything that the US government "certifies." (They also say GM foods are "safe.") But I trust Viva Labs more than I trust the US government. So who knows? I'm consuming the product along with other "good for me" supplements. I'm happy that I bought the product and paid the costly shipping fees to have it sent to me in Panama.

text: I use White Lily Flour for ALL of my cake baking. I used only Softasilk cake flour for 30 years and after trying White Lily I switched. I can use it for my most delicate cakes without them becoming fragile, such as a German Chocolate cake. I get higher volume, the flour is lighter and very soft. The softness and weight of this flour allows me to bypass any sifting because it’s not clumpy. I’ve sifted it and the cake was too light and fell during baking and cooling. It can be used it for biscuits. In my opinion it is too soft for cookies or sturdier pastries. I used to buy this flour at two stores in my area but they no longer carry it. I don’t know what the issue is regarding availability in the past year, because I can no longer find a grocer that carry’s it within a 25 mile radius of my home. The cost in the store was right in line with other flours within $1, not exceeding $4 for a 5lb bag. Ordering from this supplier has been very expensive, but still within a price point I am willing to pay because of the quality and performance of this flour. The price has risen, just like everything else these days. However, if it gets any higher I will have to stop using it, which will really devalue some of my most loved recipes.

text: Terro liquid ant cleaner works extremely well for the type of ants I have but it takes time so you need to be patient. It also tends to keep the ants away for a long time because it kills the colony. It does not work like most other ant killers that kill ants instantly. Rather it slowly poisons the ants and allows them to bring the bait back to the nest and the queen (eventually killing the queen). Over time (1-2 weeks) the ants will completely disappear. The secret is to place the bait as close to the location where the ants emerge from a wall, window, etc. When this is done the ants will focus in this area rather than all over your counter or your living space. It may take 12 hours for the ants to move away from the original food source and to the Terro spot you choose.  About 24 hours later the ants may be gone all together but don't be fooled. That is only phase one. The ants typically come back but as long as you are prepared with bait in the original location you can keep them isolated. You will have to place new bait each morning even if there are no ants because the bait dries and becomes too hard for them to take. Start with a few drops and if it draws the ants out, place additional larger drops. Let them take as much as they want them place more if they go through all the bait. text: Do not get this product.  The process of killing the ants (Borax) is fine -- however, this product suffers from two significant and serious defects.  First, the dispenser at the top is flat.  This prevents you from placing the product on a vertical surface (for example, around an outlet or on a wall).  This is a huge design flaw, and makes absolutely no sense.  The dispenser should be a tapered nozzle to allow for "aimed" application.  As a result, this product can only be used on a flat surface.  Good for the ants - bad for you.  Secondly, the consistency of the product (i.e. fluidity) is too high.  Instead of sticking to were you place it, Terro simply runs.  It eventually dries "tacky" -- but somewhere far, far away from where you put it.  Even on flat surfaces, the viscosity of the product is so high, that it simply flows away.  This could have some advantages for places the product inside an ant colony, or known "hole" -- however, because the dispenser is flat and large, there is no good way to do this.  Over all -- do not use this product.  I recommend Maggie Farm's Ant Killer -- same product, but with a good dispenser and much thicker product.

So I won't complain about the price especially considering this is better for me.  They came in little packets that were long and tubular shaped and easy to get open.  You just pop the top of your water bottle and pour the contents in, getting a little show in the meantime of the powder coming up like smoke from the bottle.  Hey, it doesn't take much to amuse me. text: I use these perfect portion sized packets on my plain low salt tortilla chips to give them that lime taste and without the salt, sugar, or other flavors that are undesired. The overall flavor is pretty close to a lime and without the bitterness that is commonly found when trying to use your own fresh limes. I appreciate the fact that there is some peel in there too. Either the lime or the lemon flavor would be useful for those who are on a low salt diet, as the citric acid naturally found in both fruits help to satisfy some of the same receptors in your mouth that salt satisfies. I use these packets to help flavor rice ramen, tacos, margaritas, and even my evening miralax water (it makes it taste so much better).  I greatly appreciate the huge box, as the smaller containers get pricey if you use a lot of them frequently. I did save 1 of the 100ct boxes as a easy go-to for quick grabs of the packets. text: Ok, I know this is a great product. Everyone raves about it, that's why I bought it. I thought everything it could do was just amazing!  Now, I have hidradenitis suppurativa, and hand eczema. Both are rare occurrences on my body, the hand eczema only when I get stressed and the HS when it feels like it, but again, it's rare.  I started with using the coconut oil on my face, my nail beds, and under my arms for deodorant because my HS really effects under my arms so I can't use regular deodorant because it blocks the pores.  After using it in those areas for a week, my face had broken out with little pimples all over my nose and chin, my hand eczema was really bad around my nail beds, and a small HS lesion had appeared under one of my arms.  I'm no dummy so I stopped using the Coconut Oil to see if it was a weird coincidence or not. After the first 3 days of not using it I could tell things were clearing up. I did nothing different in my other routines, I just stopped with the coconut oil. After a week the pimples and eczema were cleared up, it's now been 2 weeks and my lesion is gone as well.  I know I'm probably one of the rare occurrences that this happens to, but I thought that since this was natural it would help, you know? But you know, just, buy the small jar first and try it out before you end up with 32oz of something you can't use because you double dipped when applying to your underarms, no one wants to eat that.

text: I should have read the negative reviews before I bought these.  The price was great, so I impulsively bought them to fast. I have no problem with the flavors, but as everyone else has mentioned, they don't work well with Keurig.  With my first pod, the coffee was full of grounds so I had to strain it into another cup.  With the second pod, the machine was running and running and I noticed nothing coming out.  Thankfully, I stopped it in time before it blew the pod up. I figured out what the issue is - The bottom plastic of these pods is incredibly thick when you compare them to other brand pods.  So therefore, the bottom needle doesn't fully puncture the K cup, if at all.  The pod therefore fills from the top and the coffee can't get out, causing it to explode.  In order to use the remaining 98 pods that I have, I will have to open the Keurig back up after it has made its initial puncture and inspect to see if the needle went through.  If not, keep opening and closing it until you're sure the needle has gone through, then start the machine.  What a pain...not worth the extra work.  ******UPDATE:  I figured out a work around to the packaging / machine problems.  When you put the K cup in in your machine PRESS IT DOWN BY HAND TO MAKE SURE THE BOTTOM NEEDLE PENETRATES THE EXTRA THICK KCUP MATERIAL.  Then close the machine normally to make the top needle penetrate the top.  If you put the K cup in and just close the machine, there isn't enough force for the bottom needle to poke
title: UPDATE AT BOTTOM TO EVERYONE WITH MACHINE ISSUES CAUSED BY THESE K CUPS

text: Having lived the low carb lifestyle for quite a while, I had gotten used to not being able to have the food luxuries like biscuits and gravy.  The first thing made with this mix was a batch of jalapeño cheese biscuits.  When they are warm with a generous pat of butter, these biscuits taste fantastic!  It didn't take long for the first batch of biscuits to disappear in my household in spite of my eating only one per day to help keep my daily carb count in check.  So, let me just list my pros and cons of this product: Pro - If you are living the low carb lifestyle, this product will let you have your bread and eat it too. Con - If you're used to eating conventional biscuits and other bread products, the taste of this may not be that appealing to you. Pro - Can be used to make many different recipes that are otherwise flour-based. Con - 3 pound box gets used quickly experimenting with the different recipes.  And finally, one last Con - it isn't widely sold here in SoCal.  Ordering from Amazon is very convenient, but the price of the product is quite a bit more than you would pay in the supermarket for a box of biscuit mix.

text: When you visit many Southern Louisiana homes you will find certain things on the table at every meal and you will taste certain recipes that you will go home and try to replicate but can't.  You won't be able to replicate those recipes unless you go out in the gulf and catch gulf shrimp on opening day, come home, clean them and cook them right then. BUT you can get closer to the taste of the meals you have in Louisiana if you have this on your table.  This is a classic on many of the tables in many of the homes that I've been in. Salt and pepper might be on the table and salt and pepper might have their place but this is the first thing you reach for if your going to season your dish. Cajun seasoning to those in Louisiana is like green chile to those of us in New Mexico- a necessary staple.  The yellow container is hot and the red container is hotter. You use this on just about everything. Your eggs, your steak, your salad and so on. It just adds that extra kick to whatever your eating.  Personally, after trying many varieties of Cajun seasoning, this one is one of my favorites. It has a kick but it is not so hot that all you taste is your burned mouth and a charred tongue after it bursts into flames. It is flavorful and full bodied.  Enjoy.
title: A classic Cajun Staple

text: This is actually my first review ever for a product.  What inspired me to review was not the product (although it is also worthy), but rather the customer service.  I received an excellent product on my first order.  Unfortunately, my second order had an issue with one of the bags.  I contacted People's Choice on a weekend, and received a prompt response from Megan.  She let me know that problems can unfortunately arise due to a preservative-free product and offered to send a replacement bag, or a refund.  I opted for the replacement bag (which Megan said she would personally inspect to ensure it met their standards).  The replacement bag arrived in short order and was as good (if not better) than the first bag I ordered.  As a small service-oriented business owner myself, I understand that it is the people and customer service as much as the product that make for a successful business.  I commend them on both their product and their team and can't wait to place my next order.  I also think that people too often focus on the negatives, and need to hear what companies do when problems arise.  Please do not hesitate ordering from People's Choice. text: These freeze-dried Skittles are crunchy, with the sweet and tart fruity flavors of Skittles that you would expect. The freeze-drying process removes all chewiness from the candy, leaving you with concentrated flavor that melts on the tongue and does not stick to your teeth. I like these candies and would recommend them as a novelty gift and/or a way for someone who can't have chewy candy (such as those with dentures or possibly even braces) to enjoy a fun treat.

text: This is a review of "Snack Hut Astro Snax Freeze Dried Skittles Candy Original Fruit Flavors Freeze Dried in the USA - Freeze Dried Candy Variety Pack Dry Freeze Candy - Great Gift for Men Women & Children on any Occasion"  I am an undisputed expert on freeze dried foods that astronauts eat. Not that I have been to space, ever. But I have been to all the space museums in the US and have always bought the freeze dried foods that they offer in the souvenir stores. They are always disappointing. Example: Freeze dried vanilla ice cream is tastes like paper and crumbles like dust.  This product under review is my first freeze dried candy and more specifically, this particular product is freeze dried skittled candy. Now, I have to be honest, I do not like skittles at all. It is hard and you cannot tell one flavor from another. It is basically a sugar ball without any character and has only color to go by.  This is where this freeze dried version of skittles changes the game altogether. The skittles balls apparently explode when freeze drying leading to the candy exploding like a popcorn. The result? Each flavor is distinct and elaborately bought out. I certainly did not expect this result of freeze drying. So it does work as a novelty gift. It may also work in high altitudes or hard climates too. Surely this is not for the mass market given the price, but it is a delightful product and is perfect as a novelty food item. I think the price is  bit steep but I liked it a lot given how
title: Out of this world freeze dried candy!

text: I love skittles, so it's hard not to enjoy these. They are airy, light, and crisp. The same skittles taste is there. I get the novelty of it and it's worth trying. I think these are probably great for people who don't like the chewy texture and like the "crispness" of it. It comes at a premium, but it is what they say it is...freeze dried skittles....and they were fresh.
title: Novel, Puffy, CRISP, Sweet. All about texture.

text: As a science nerd, I was excited to try this candy. What chemistry geek doesn't want food tossed in liquid nitrogen? (I assume that's how these were made.) However cool (get it?) the concept is, the candy itself is not that good. Eating it is like eating vaguely skittle-tasting sugar cubes. text: Snack Hut Astro Snax Freeze dried skittles candy6oz. They arrived quickly and from a USA-based, family owned company. The bag isn’t “huge”, but it is a decent size and came 2/3rds full(settling happens, I know). I think the planets and little astronaut design is adorable and awesome.  This was my first time trying something freeze dried so I was stoked. These are very sweet and crispy. The freeze drying process strips away the moisture which makes these more concentrated and sweeter. And you definitely will taste it! For me they were a little bit on the too sweet side so I can only eat a couple per sitting. Conversely, that does help curb my munchies, which is a plus.  I think the price(12.99) is very fair and comparable to what I’ve seen locally. These would be great for kids or those with teeth problems or if you’re a person who like that tang sweet skittles flavor but not the chewiness. It’s great they don’t stick to your teeth. I would recommend this brand and try more from them.

text: I had never tried toasted sesame oil before testing this product through Amazon Vine, but this product has made me a convert! The taste is sublime! Unlike regular sesame oil, toasted sesame oil is extracted from roasted sesame seeds. The roasting process causes the resulting oil to be darker in color and thicker in consistency. Best of all, it creates a deeper, richer flavor.  Before cooking with this toasted sesame oil, I did some research and learned that it has a much lower smoke point than regular sesame oil. This means that it will burn and become nasty tasting if you cook with it, even at a low temperature. For this reason, it is not suitable for frying. However, it is an outstanding condiment, with some really terrific applications that I tested out and loved, including:  1. A topping for ginger-garlic noodle soup. I also sprinkled some sesame seeds on top of the soup for additional sesame flavor and crunch. Yum!  2. After cooking vegetable stir fry with regular sesame oil, when I took it off the heat, I drizzled some of this toasted sesame oil on it, and stirred well until all of the vegetables were coated with it. Delicious!  3. I made a marinade with this oil, ginger, tamari soy sauce and a little peanut butter. I then used it to coat udon noodles. Outstanding!  I will definitely purchase more of this oil in the future, and will happily recommend it to friends and family.

Citric acid is used in the biotechnology and pharmaceuticals industries to passivate stainless steel processing piping and vessels and to remove minerals and trace iron from water distillation equipment so it is very safe to use.  If propperly diluted at one pound of citric acid powder to three gallons of city water it is very much like many citrus carbonated soft drinks.  It is less expansive to use than distilled white vinegar and more effective for cleaning and maintaining our tankless water heater.

text: I like coffee that tastes like coffee beans, not like emaciated grocery store brands from the Fifties. I’ve always thought Starbucks fresh coffee tastes “burnt” so I stopped going there in favor of “The Human Bean” in Phoenix. And after reading about the owner of Starbucks, I did this subjective taste test to try and find an instant I could live with to “instantly” move away from giving my money to Starbucks Via.  In my comparison of five brands, I used one teaspoon of instant and ¾ cup of hot water in each brand, kept it just black, and tasted it hot. Next, I added one teaspoon of heavy cream and 10 drops of Sweet Leaf brand vanilla-flavored extract and tasted it hot. Then, I waited until it cooled to room temp and tasted it again. Here are my personal findings with 5 being “worst”:  5. Waka Decaf – Slightly sour and brackish, tastes “instant” and gets worse as it cools. An absolute “no.” (1 packet per 8-10 oz.) 4. Jacobs Espresso – Watery, thin, and so “smooth” as to be tasteless, and they have the nerve to call this “espresso”? (No English instructions I could find—I guess they didn’t think it was worth the bother—and they’re probably right.) 3. Mt. Hagen Espresso – Also too smooth and lacking in taste, but has a wee more grunt and flavour than Jacobs. (1 packet per cup—I assume they mean 8 oz.) 2. Café Bustelo Espresso – Definitely better than the others but still “middle of the road” when it comes to true bean flavour. At least it tastes like coffee, even when cool. 1. V

text: I'll be honest, I have a big sweet tooth so none of these unsweetened coffee creamers, regardless of the brand, are appealing to me. With that being said, my blood sugar level rose according to my last blood test (surprise, surprise) so I haaaaad to switch to an unsweetened version. So far, Nutpods have been my favorite go-to coffee creamer (the almond + coconut ones, haven't tried their oatmilk creamers). The coconut cream adds a bit of creaminess that kind of (and I mean, kind of) offsets the lack of sweetness for me, and the added almonds don't weigh down my stomach compared to straight coconut milk.  I saw this new(?) flavor on Amazon, coffee cake, and wanted to try it. As for flavor. there is a slight cinnamony taste with a somewhat tangy after taste, as some reviews have mentioned. As for size, I was surprised to see how small they were (11.2oz x 3) since my first Nutpods purchase was the 25.4oz at a local store (and I thought that was small, too, since I used to buy the 32oz sweetened almond milk creamer of another brand). I still want to try other Nutpods flavors, but for me, I really don't taste much difference, whether it's coffee cake, French vanilla, or whatever, since it's hard for me to taste them as unsweetened desserts, if that makes any sense. Maybe I'll appreciate the flavors more as I get used to drinking unsweetened coffee...
title: Smaller than expected

text: This is not gourmet cocoa; none of the cocoas easily purchased for the Keurig system are outstanding cocoas.  These drinks are sweetened with artificial sweeteners (Splenda).  They do taste like that.  People who prefer not to use artificial sweeteners should avoid these.  Having said that, the cocoas are a great way for kids >age 8 to serve themselves, adjusting how large they would like their cups, and adding milk if needed.  For added flavor, plop a square of Hershey's chocolate at the bottom of the cup.  This purchase is good value compared to purchasing in the supermarket.  Our favorite hot chocolates are made by melting a square of Hershey's milk chocolate in a cup of milk.  Simple, delicious, real ingredients.  It does take a stove top and is a bit inconvenient.  The other hot chocolate that is good is the Starbuck line of hot chocolates.  Fresh Market and William Sonoma carry powdered hot chocolate that is also very good, but more expensive.

text: Prior to ordering this large resealable bag of Blue Diamond Oven Roasted Dark Chocolate Almonds, I read the ingredient list and was aware that one of the last ingredients is Stevia.  The Blue Diamond has the following ingredients list:  ALMONDS, SUGAR, COCOA POWDER (PROCESSED WITH ALKALI), CORN MALTODEXTRIN, NATURAL FLAVOR, SEA SALT, REBIANA (STEVIA EXTRACT).  I love Blue Diamond Almonds but I don't love these.  They are fresh, tasty, flavorful roasted almonds as the base, but because the Stevia is a stronger taste than the cocoa coating, there is an unappealing taste that outweighs the almonds and the chocolate.  If you've ever had a prepared package of sugar-free hot chocolate or coffee, you know what I'm talking about.  This is not even a good option for those who are on a sugar-free diet for health reasons or simply by choice because sugar is listed as the second ingredient and precedes cocoa powder.  I thought they would have a bittersweet cocoa flavor and actually wondered why refined Stevia was included when I read the list, but I'm not a chemist or food scientist, so I ordered the nuts, assuming it was to reduce the sugar calories.  Unfortunately, the Stevia taste is more forward, middle, and end in the taste profile of these nuts, overpowering the cocoa and they are a disappointment.  Nevertheless, they are Blue Diamond almonds and the actual nuts are firm and the thin shell of coating has a good texture.  I just don't like the lingering unnatural taste of the added
title: Strong taste of Stevia

text: These dark roast flavors are truly robust and rounded with my favorite aspects of darker roast coffees.  It seems that there's no compromise for quality with what would otherwise be a taste akin to standard pot coffee (bleh!).  Rich, full bodied and potent, these two flavors hit the mark on what should be expected for intensity.  That said, my favorite brand excels with being able to make even espresso roast smoother than these - though I'm not saying these are astringent or too bold.  I just know there can be a finer balance that I think is missing in both flavors.  Nespresso kindly color codes their packaging and capsules with lighter colors for lighter roasts and darker colors for darker roasts.  The packaging itself is beautiful, however I am not a big fan of capsules since they consume so much material and space, as well as additional packaging.  I truly think the best option is loose bean/grinds that can be used in machine adapters or with alternative brew methods.  The saving on material and storage space also translates to saved $ on coffee... which I think Nespresso could embrace with standalone coffee sales (some of their flavors are worth it). Fortunately, you can recycle capsules (and of course packaging) locally or send capsules back to Nespresso where they'll recycle them.  Tip of the hat to that free service Nespresso.  = )
title: Nice dark roast pack
